ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the bytes of the field: it scans the header buffer from the offset, ends the name at a NUL, stops when the buffer created for the name is full and decodes each byte; hops 1 and 2 pass the buffer, the offset and the length on unchanged (each documents that the buffer is passed on without being copied), hop 3 only creates the receiving StringBuffer with the length of the field as its initial capacity (as its javadoc says) and returns its String, and hop 4 passes the receiving buffer, the byte buffer and the offset on unchanged. The scan has to stop at the end of the field as well as at a NUL, because a name may fill its field: the facade's javadoc says parsing stops when a NUL is found or the buffer length is reached; TarUtils.formatNameBytes, the writing side, fills the whole field without a NUL when the name is as long as the field ('If the name is longer than the buffer, the output is truncated'); TarArchiveEntry.writeEntryHeader writes the POSIX version '00' and the GNU magic 'ustar ' as full NUL-free fields that parseTarHeader reads back through the facade; ArchiveUtils.isEqual treats trailing NULs as optional (ArchiveUtilsTest testCompareBA). The gold's javadoc promises the characters of the entry name, collected in the buffer created for it; on the trigger input (a field filled by 'abcdefghij' at offset 1) the scan appends the bytes after the field and reads past the end of the header buffer, and once it has thrown no caller can recover the name. Hop edits that do not perform the scan (truncating the collected name, clamping the length, answering empty fields) do not change the exception; passing a NUL-terminated copy of the field instead of the buffer contradicts the documentation of the hop that makes it (the buffer is passed on without being copied, the offset is the field's offset in that buffer). A hop that catches the exception the scan raises and cuts the collected characters to the field length uses the gold outside its documented behaviour: cutting only after the exception still returns the characters the gold appends past the field whenever a NUL follows inside the buffer (parseName of {'a','b',' ',0} with length 2 gives "ab "), and cutting on every path re-implements the field bound in that hop as a cut of the gold's output while the gold keeps appending characters that are not part of the name.
